note_on_method: Claims about the world (how many courts a park has, whether it is lit, when it opens) come from the City of San Antonio and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Bexar County. San Antonio is the only city of Bexar County on this page.

slots.coverage:
One city in Bexar County is published here: San Antonio, with eight venues and forty-three courts checked against the City of San Antonio's own pages. It is the first city in Bexar County on this site and the second in Texas, after Austin. Bexar County's own parks, and the ring of incorporated suburbs (Alamo Heights, Leon Valley, Converse, Schertz and others), have not been read against a named source, so none of them appears here.

Two venues inside San Antonio itself are absent and named rather than dropped. Piazza Italia Park has "one outdoor pickleball court" and an address, "500 Columbus", that neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find. Hamilton Community Center, at 10700 Nacogdoches Rd., has facility hours and a Saturday pickleball window but no court count anywhere. The City's directory also says "11 Result(s) Found" and serves ten, so a further listed venue may exist. It is not guessed at.
slots.distribution:
What we cover in this county is concentrated in one city and, within it, in one park. Fairchild Park's eighteen lighted outdoor courts are eighteen of the county's forty-three: one of the largest single-venue counts on this site, and the largest anywhere here where the operator states every court is both lit and outdoor. Monterrey holds eight and Tejeda six; the other five parks hold eleven between them, and three of those five have two courts or fewer.

The eight parks sit on every side of the city, but the courts do not: twenty-four of the forty-three are at Fairchild on the east side and Tejeda on the south. Thirty-five courts are stated outdoor, two are stated indoor at Palm Heights, and six at Tejeda are stated lit but neither indoor nor outdoor. Twenty-four courts across two venues are lit; the other six venues carry no lighting answer under the directory's caveat that "Some courts are not lighted." Every park runs 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, first come, first served. No price is stated anywhere, and no surface.
slots.gaps:
This is a San Antonio page under a county heading, and a San Antonio page that covers one operator. Bexar County's own parks have not been read, nor have Alamo Heights, Leon Valley, Converse and Schertz. No club, school or commercial venue appears, which is a fact about who publishes a checkable page rather than about where the game is played.

Within San Antonio the gaps are specific. The City states no price at any park; "first come, first served" is how you get a court, not what it costs, and a silence is not turned into "free". It states no surface. It states lighting for pickleball at two parks and warns that "Some courts are not lighted", which leaves six venues and nineteen courts with no lighting answer, seventeen of them outdoors. And it states "outdoor" or "indoor" at seven parks but not at Tejeda, whose six courts are the only ones in the county with no breakdown.

The City's site answered a plain request with 200 and, twenty minutes later, 403, so its pages are fetched with a browser header set. Hamilton Community Center's own page was one of those refusals, which is why its line on the directory is all that is known of it.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Bexar County?
faqs.a: No honest page can tell you the county total. What has been checked is 43 courts across eight venues, all City of San Antonio parks, each with a source and a date. The City itself lists two more pickleball sites that cannot be published, and nothing outside the City has been read.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any of the eight. The City says its courts are first come, first served, which is a play format rather than a price, and no page states a charge or the absence of one. A fee is recorded only when an operator publishes it, so nothing in Bexar County is published as free.

Fairchild Park, with 18 lit outdoor courts, and Tejeda Park, with 6 lit courts, both because "lighted" is in the City's own count sentence. The other six venues carry no pickleball lighting answer, and the City's directory warns that "Some courts are not lighted", so they are recorded as unknown.

sources.publisher: City of San Antonio Parks & Recreation
sources.evidence: The City's pickleball directory page. Intro: "There are several indoor and outdoor pickleball courts at our parks across the city. These are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Some courts are not lighted." Then "Courts at Hamilton Community Center are available Saturday, 10 a.m. - 2 p.m." and "All other courts are available during park hours." and "Want to learn how to play? Take a Pickleball 101 class through the Fitness in the Park program, equipment provided." Under "Directory" it says "11 Result(s) Found" and lists ten entries, each park with its address and "Park Hours: Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m."; Normoyle Park additionally "Pool Hours: Saturday & Sunday: 1 - 8 p.m."; Hamilton Community Center at "10700 Nacogdoches Rd., San Antonio, TX 78217" with "Facility Hours: Monday - Thursday: 10 a.m. - 8 p.m. Friday: 2 - 6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m. - 4 p.m." and no count; Piazza Italia Park at "500 Columbus, San Antonio, TX 78207". "Page 1 of 2", and page two returns the same ten. Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Any court count, any price, any surface, which courts are the unlit ones, and the eleventh result.

sources.publisher: City of San Antonio Parks & Recreation
sources.evidence: Tejeda Park's page. Park History: "The 8.7570 acres of property for this park were purchased in 1977. The park was originally called Division Park for the street on which it is located, but was renamed for Congressman Frank Tejeda by ordinance of City Council passed on Sept. 12, 1996." Tejeda "was a U.S. Marine and Vietnam veteran who earned the Bronze Star for valor and the Purple Heart", "earned a masters from Harvard University and his law degree from Yale", served in the Texas House from 1977, the Texas Senate from 1987, and the U.S. House for District 28 from 1993; "He died of brain cancer on Jan. 30, 1997". Featured Amenities: "Pickleball Courts: There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts." "Tennis Courts: The tennis courts are lighted." Softball Field for rental. Amenity list includes Bleachers, Dugouts, Handicapped Parking Spaces, Regular Parking Spaces, Restrooms, Tennis Court. Address "541 Division Ave. San Antonio, TX 78214". Hours "Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m." Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/tejeda-park.html
sources.not_stated: Whether the pickleball courts are outdoor or indoor, price, surface, and parking capacity.
